description: Hierarchical, temporal, multi-label intent ontology for the Shenji dataset. v2.0.0 adds four judgment status layers (BACKGROUND, UNKNOWN, AMBIGUOUS, OUT_OF_ONTOLOGY), field-level annotation criteria per intent, and a confusion resolution matrix for easily confused pairs.
changelog_v2: Added four non-tactical judgment status layers (NOT in parent hierarchy): BACKGROUND, UNKNOWN, AMBIGUOUS, OUT_OF_ONTOLOGY

Each intent now has: necessary_conditions, sufficient_evidence, counterexamples, hard_negative, allowed_cooccurrence, conflicts_with, primary_vs_secondary, minimum_duration, boundary_rules, applicable_subject_scope
Added confusion resolution matrix for ASSAULT/SEIZE, HOLD/FORTIFY, RECON/SURVEILLANCE, RETREAT/EVADE, FLANK/BREAKTHROUGH, FIRE_SUPPORT/main_task
FEINT remains Grade C with requires_plan_tag=true; failed attack must NOT be derived as FEINT

status_layers.definition: Purposeful movement or behavior that serves no identifiable tactical intent from the observer's perspective. Examples: routine repositions, route transit through non-threat areas, administrative moves.
status_layers.relation_to_tactical_hierarchy: independent — coexists alongside the six parent categories; a segment may be BACKGROUND in one track (commanded) while having tactical intent in another (realized).

status_layers.definition: Available evidence is insufficient to assign any tactical intent with confidence above the rejection threshold. The observer sees behavior but cannot determine its purpose.
status_layers.relation_to_tactical_hierarchy: independent — used when the total evidence weight for all tactical categories falls below the decision threshold.

status_layers.definition: Evidence supports two or more conflicting tactical intents with comparable strength, and the observer cannot resolve which applies.
status_layers.relation_to_tactical_hierarchy: independent — used when the highest two posterior probabilities are within a tie margin of each other.

status_layers.definition: Observed behavior pattern does not conform to any of the 22 defined tactical intents. Applied to emergent or novel behaviors not anticipated by the ontology.
status_layers.relation_to_tactical_hierarchy: independent — signals a coverage gap in the ontology.

confusion_matrix.discrimination_key: ASSAULT targets enemy combatants for destruction; SEIZE targets terrain/objectives for control.
confusion_matrix.notes: A coordinated assault on a defended objective may combine both.

confusion_matrix.discrimination_key: HOLD is area control over a designated objective; FORTIFY is a posture (concealment, fortification) that may support HOLD but is not equivalent.
confusion_matrix.notes: Can be sequential: FORTIFY at a position then HOLD it.

confusion_matrix.discrimination_key: RECON is active search into unknown space; SURVEILLANCE is persistent observation of a known target/area.
confusion_matrix.notes: A unit may transition from RECON to SURVEILLANCE after detecting the target.

confusion_matrix.discrimination_key: RETREAT is sustained disengagement from the principal threat; EVADE is a short defensive maneuver after which the unit returns to the original task.
FLANK bypasses the front to attack laterally; BREAKTHROUGH pushes through a frontal defensive line.
confusion_matrix.notes: Combined operation: flanking force + frontal breakthrough.

confusion_matrix.discrimination_key: FIRE_SUPPORT is always secondary to a supported task. If fire is the unit's sole observable purpose, consider ASSAULT or INTERDICT instead.
confusion_matrix.notes: FIRE_SUPPORT must co-occur with at least one other intent.

intents.definition: Directly close with and attack a designated enemy or defended objective.
exclusions: contact caused only by route crossing
necessary_conditions: Approach vector points toward known enemy or objective within engagement range
At least one SHOOT or close-combat event during approach
sufficient_evidence: mission_type=0 command + MOVE-toward + SHOOT sequence
counterexamples: Movement toward enemy without engagement (RECON)
Long-range fire without closure (FIRE_SUPPORT)
hard_negative: FEINT with similar approach trajectory but early disengagement before SHOOT range
intents.boundary_rules: After first SHOOT within approach context, duration extends until target eliminated or unit shifts to new sector.

intents.definition: Force passage through a defended line, choke point, or blocking force.
necessary_conditions: Unit crosses a defensive line held by enemy
Enemy attempts to block passage (SHOOT or HOLD posture detected)
sufficient_evidence: Boundary crossing under enemy fire + continued forward progress
counterexamples: Routine road movement through unopposed terrain
hard_negative: FLANK with crossing of a weak point not actively defended
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when approach to defensive line begins; ends when passage is achieved or unit is repelled.

intents.definition: Bypass the frontal axis and approach a target from a lateral or rear sector.
operational_criteria: terminal approach from flank or rear
necessary_conditions: Unit path deviates from direct approach to bypass a known defensive position
Terminal bearing to target differs from initial bearing by > 45 degrees
sufficient_evidence: Flank-path geometry + engagement from lateral/rear sector
counterexamples: Path deviation due to terrain obstacle, not enemy presence
hard_negative: BREAKTHROUGH with frontal approach (no flank angle)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when deviation from direct approach begins; ends when target is engaged or flank attempt abandoned.

intents.definition: Multiple friendly elements reduce a target's escape space from distinct sectors.
necessary_conditions: At least 2 friendly units approach from directions separated by > 90 degrees
Units maintain positional advantage relative to target
sufficient_evidence: Multi-sector convergence + persistent containment (angular gap < 90 deg for > 5 steps)
counterexamples: Multiple units approaching from same sector (single-axis assault)
hard_negative: Two units independently chasing the same target without coordination (PURSUIT)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when second unit enters a distinct approach sector; ends when encirclement is achieved or broken.

intents.definition: Maintain contact with and attack an enemy that is withdrawing.
exclusions: independent movement in the same direction
necessary_conditions: Target shows RETREAT or EVADE pattern
Friendly unit follows with correlated path
sufficient_evidence: Correlated pursuit trajectory + engagement during withdrawal
counterexamples: Unit moving in same direction as enemy without knowing enemy position (REDEPLOY)
hard_negative: Bounding overwatch advance (ASSAULT technique, not PURSUIT)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when target begins withdrawal and pursuer follows; ends when target is destroyed, escapes, or engagement stops.

intents.definition: Wait in concealment or a prepared position and initiate attack after a trigger.
exclusions: ordinary static defense without a trigger
necessary_conditions: Unit occupies concealed or fortified position before enemy arrival
First SHOOT occurs within short interval of enemy entering engagement range
sufficient_evidence: FORTIFY or stationary wait > 3 steps + enemy arrival + immediate engagement
counterexamples: Static defensive position that fires on any approaching enemy (HOLD)
hard_negative: HOLD at a defensive position where enemy happens to approach
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when unit enters concealed position with no enemy in engagement range; ends when enemy is engaged or ambush abandoned.

intents.definition: Take control of an enemy or neutral objective.
exclusions: passing through an objective without occupation
necessary_conditions: Unit targets a specific objective (building, city, control point)
Occupation action (type 5) or ownership change detected
sufficient_evidence: Action type 5 on objective
counterexamples: Movement through a city without stopping (REDEPLOY)
hard_negative: FEINT toward objective with no occupation attempt
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts at first approach step toward objective; ends when occupation action completes or attempt fails.

intents.definition: Maintain control of a friendly objective or assigned area against threat.
exclusions: idle presence without assigned control responsibility
necessary_conditions: Unit is positioned at a friendly or designated objective
Enemy attempts to approach or capture
sufficient_evidence: mission_type=1 + stationary at objective + enemy engagement
counterexamples: Unit waiting at a waypoint without engagement (BACKGROUND)
hard_negative: FORTIFY at a non-objective location without enemy contact
intents.boundary_rules: Segment persists while unit holds radius and enemy threat is present; ends when unit leaves or threat is eliminated.

intents.definition: Block, delay, or channel enemy movement through a route or region.
exclusions: static defense unrelated to enemy movement
necessary_conditions: Unit is positioned at a known passage or choke point
Enemy attempts transit through that passage
sufficient_evidence: Choke-point positioning + fire or obstacle that delays known enemy movement
counterexamples: Static guard at a non-choke-point location (HOLD)
hard_negative: HOLD at a general defensive line (no choke-point specificity)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when enemy approach to choke point is detected; ends when enemy is stopped, diverted, or passage is lost.

intents.definition: Actively search unknown space or locate enemy forces.
operational_criteria: move through unobserved or assigned search region
exclusions: movement whose primary objective is attack or withdrawal
necessary_conditions: Unit enters territory without prior enemy detection
Unit generates new detection events
sufficient_evidence: mission_type=2 + path through unobserved territory + new detections
counterexamples: Movement through already-observed territory (REDEPLOY)
hard_negative: SURVEILLANCE with no search movement (persistent observation of known target)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when unit enters unobserved area; ends when search objective is met or unit transitions to engagement.

intents.definition: Persistently observe a known target or area while avoiding unnecessary engagement.
necessary_conditions: Unit maintains sight of a known target for > 5 consecutive steps
Engagement rate (SHOOT events / observation steps) < 0.2
sufficient_evidence: Persistent LOS to same target + low engagement ratio
counterexamples: Unit that detects and immediately engages (ASSAULT)
hard_negative: RECON patrolling that happens to maintain LOS briefly
intents.primary_vs_secondary: primary, may be secondary to TARGET_GUIDANCE
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when persistent observation pattern (> 5 steps) is established; ends when LOS is lost or unit transitions to engagement.

intents.definition: Provide target information or correction support for another firing element.
operational_criteria: observer and firing element are distinct
guidance contributes to a fire event
necessary_conditions: Action type 9 emitted with guided_obj_id set
A separate unit fires at guided target
sufficient_evidence: Action type 9 + guided_fire event on target
counterexamples: Direct fire without guidance (ASSAULT)
hard_negative: FIRE_SUPPORT on called-in coordinates without active guidance link
intents.primary_vs_secondary: secondary only (always supports a firing element)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment spans the guidance action and the resulting guided fire event.

intents.definition: Move toward a friendly element or area under pressure to increase combat power.
necessary_conditions: Friendly unit is in contact with enemy
Reinforcing unit moves toward the contact area
sufficient_evidence: Movement vector toward friendly contact + arrival within engagement range + subsequent coordinated fire
counterexamples: Unit moving past a friendly contact without participating (REDEPLOY)
hard_negative: REDEPLOY into same area for independent reasons (no support intent)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when reinforcing unit begins movement toward beneficiary; ends when arrival and coordinated action complete.

intents.definition: Accompany and protect a designated friendly unit or formation.
necessary_conditions: Two units maintain bounded proximity (< 3 hexes) for > 5 consecutive steps
Escorting unit engages threats approaching the beneficiary
sufficient_evidence: Formation persistence + defensive engagement on behalf of beneficiary
counterexamples: Units moving together without defensive responsibility (co-located REDEPLOY)
hard_negative: ASSEMBLE then movement together (formation transit, not ESCORT)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when escort formation is established; ends when formation breaks or escort task is completed.

intents.definition: Apply direct, indirect, or suppressive fire in support of another friendly task.
operational_criteria: fire affects its target or approach
necessary_conditions: Firing unit is not the primary assaulter/approacher
A supported friendly unit is engaging the same target or sector
sufficient_evidence: Action type 8 (indirect) or type 9 (guided) + support relation to another unit's action
counterexamples: Unit firing in self-defense (ASSAULT component)
hard_negative: ASSAULT that includes fire as part of its own approach
intents.primary_vs_secondary: secondary only (must co-occur with at least one other intent)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment spans the fire support action(s). Must NOT be the only intent assigned to a segment.

intents.definition: Move from one task sector or posture to another without immediate contact as the primary purpose.
necessary_conditions: Unit moves > 5 hexes without enemy contact
No enemy within observation range during movement
sufficient_evidence: Long-range non-contact movement + sector change
counterexamples: Movement to contact (ASSAULT initial phase)
hard_negative: RETREAT with similar movement but under enemy contact
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when unit leaves previous sector; ends when unit arrives at new sector or makes contact.

intents.definition: Converge multiple units or aggregate sub-elements into a formation.
necessary_conditions: At least 2 friendly units decrease pairwise distance
Action type 15 or 315 emitted
sufficient_evidence: Action type 15/315 + converging trajectories
counterexamples: Single unit waiting (not ASSEMBLE)
hard_negative: DISPERSE followed by incidental proximity
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when converge begins; ends when assembly is complete or cancelled.

intents.definition: Separate a formation or increase spacing to reduce concentration or expand coverage.
exclusions: formation breakup caused by unit destruction
necessary_conditions: At least 2 friendly units increase pairwise distance
Action type 14 or 314 emitted
sufficient_evidence: Action type 14/314 + diverging trajectories
counterexamples: Unit destruction causing separation (not DISPERSE)
hard_negative: RETREAT splitting formation (dispersal due to flight, not tactical intent)
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when divergence begins; ends when dispersion target is reached.

intents.definition: Adopt concealment, prepared defense, or fortification occupancy.
exclusions: brief stop caused by route completion
necessary_conditions: Unit enters concealed state (move_state=4) or occupies fortification
Unit remains in fortified posture > 2 steps
sufficient_evidence: move_state=4 or action type 18 + sustained stationary posture
counterexamples: Brief stop for route planning (1 step, no concealment)
hard_negative: HOLD posture at objective without entering concealed state
intents.primary_vs_secondary: primary, may be secondary to HOLD or AMBUSH
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when concealment/fortification state is entered; ends when unit leaves state.

intents.definition: Sustainably disengage from contact and increase separation from the principal threat.
necessary_conditions: Unit was in contact with enemy
Unit moves away from threat for > 3 consecutive steps with increasing separation
sufficient_evidence: Post-contact withdrawal + persistent separation growth > 3 steps
counterexamples: REDEPLOY away from a sector without enemy contact
hard_negative: EVADE that returns to original task after brief threat avoidance
intents.boundary_rules: Segment starts when unit turns away from contact; ends when separation plateaus or unit exits threat area.

intents.definition: Temporarily alter movement or posture to avoid a threat without abandoning the broader task.
operational_criteria: return to task or route afterward
necessary_conditions: Unit makes abrupt bearing change (> 60 degrees in 1-2 steps)
Unit returns to prior task direction within 5 steps
sufficient_evidence: Abrupt threat-avoidance maneuver + return to prior heading
counterexamples: Sustained withdrawal (RETREAT)
hard_negative: Obstacle avoidance without enemy threat
intents.primary_vs_secondary: primary, may be secondary to another intent
intents.boundary_rules: EVADE of > 5 steps should be reclassified as RETREAT.

intents.definition: Present misleading movement or attack evidence to induce an incorrect adversary assessment.
operational_criteria: observable false cue differs from hidden main task
necessary_conditions: Plan tag explicitly marks this segment as FEINT
Failed attack without plan tag must NOT be labeled FEINT
sufficient_evidence: Plan tag + human reviewer confirmation
counterexamples: Failed attack that was intended as genuine (not FEINT)
hard_negative: Failed ASSAULT with similar approach trajectory but no deceptive plan tag
intents.boundary_rules: Only labeled via plan tag + human review. Behavior alone is never sufficient for FEINT.
